t: Fayetteville schedules a hearing on a data center moratorium after a 6–4 vote
b: The divided council also voted to keep drafting regulations; the city has debated the issue for months, and Cumberland County's pause does not cover city limits.

t: Stafford approves the Accokeek Center data center campus, 4–3
b: The rezoning allows about 590,000 sq ft on 121 acres with roughly $6.4 million in developer contributions and limits on water use, despite a crowd opposed to the project.

t: Spanberger's energy plan asks data centers to cover the cost increases they cause
b: The long-term plan, unveiled with her budget, also leans on solar and storage and needs legislation in 2027; Republicans said it would raise costs.
iw: Proposed cost shift to data centers

t: Virginia cites Google's first Chesterfield data center site for seven runoff violations
b: The notice documents sediment discharges between December 2025 and August 2026 affecting thousands of feet of stream channel and about 1.4 acres of wetlands; Google blamed heavy rain.

t: Lovejoy bans data centers citywide
b: The ban followed opposition to Stillwater Development's proposed 3.5 million sq ft campus near schools and repealed a permit path that would have allowed them.

t: Virginia proposes a record $2.5 million penalty for a Microsoft data center
b: A June 2025 substation failure left the Leesburg site running 62 diesel generators for a week, pushing it past permit limits. Microsoft agreed to fund expanded air monitoring; public comment closed Oct. 14.

t: Holly Springs, Spring Hope, Boiling Spring Lakes, Hillsborough and Southport pause data centers
b: Spring Hope acted in May; Holly Springs, Boiling Spring Lakes and Hillsborough in June; and Southport on Sept. 10 with no project proposed.

t: Marietta, Walker County, Forest Park and Americus adopt data center pauses
b: Walker County began with a 30-day pause on July 10, Marietta's runs through Dec. 31, Forest Park approved 90 days and Americus 30 days on Sept. 24.

t: Mercer County rejects rules that would have allowed hyperscale data centers
b: The unanimous voice vote blocked siting next to a coal plant near Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill; nearby Burgin is weighing annexation for a hyperscale project.

t: Senator's poll finds 55% of his Madison County district oppose more data centers
b: Givhan's survey of his Huntsville-area district came as north Alabama debates new data centers under TVA's new data center rates.

t: Calvert County pauses data center site plans after Amazon drops its project
b: Amazon withdrew its Calvert Technology Center plan in early August following voter backlash in the June primary; the six-month moratorium took effect Aug. 28.

t: Cary adopts an 18-month data center pause
b: Staff will study power demand, water use, noise and site design, with the council expected to revisit the issue in February 2028.

t: Asheville, Woodfin, Franklin and Jackson County pause data centers
b: Woodfin acted in May, Asheville unanimously in June, Franklin in July and Jackson County on Aug. 18, each for about a year.

t: Alabama Power files data center contracts with key terms blacked out
b: Filings for Meta- and Nebius-linked projects hide contract length, power amounts, prices and minimum bills, though the utility says each deal covers its own costs.

t: Kent County adopts data center rules with a 55-decibel cap, 7–0
b: The ordinance limits where facilities can go, requires plans for water, power, cooling and cleanup, and orders removal within 180 days after a year of disuse.

t: Douglas County rejects a 4.4 million sq ft campus near Villa Rica, 4–1
b: The EdgeConneX-linked plan for about 700 acres had shrunk from an earlier 11-building proposal; the planning commission recommended denial and residents played noise demonstrations.

t: Nelson and Boyd counties pause data centers; Georgetown backs a Scott County pause
b: Boyd's six-month moratorium, adopted July 9, exempts the already-planned Muskie campus.

t: Bowling Green adopts data center standards after rejecting a moratorium
b: Ordinance BG2026-6 sets rules on energy and water demand, noise, light, setbacks and site design.

t: Cumberland County pauses data centers for six months, 7–0
b: The ban on site plan reviews and permits runs to Dec. 15 while staff write rules on water, power, noise and distance from homes, schools and Fort Bragg.

t: Durham extends its data center pause to a full year
b: The council first passed a 60-day moratorium on May 4, then unanimously added 10 months; Durham County later matched it through May 2027.

t: Hundreds of thousands sign a petition against a data center near the Nashville Zoo
b: More than 150 people also spoke against proposals near the zoo and Fisk University at a June planning meeting, before the city paused data center permits.

t: Daviess County adopts a 12-month data center moratorium
b: Residents pushed for the pause after news of a hyperscale project planned at an idled aluminum mill in neighboring Hancock County.

t: Cave City pauses data centers for a year; a developer sues
b: Kentucky Industrial Alliance, which had filed plans for 318 acres, sued June 8; the Kentucky League of Cities is helping fund the city's defense.

t: Harnett County adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: The pause came amid a Triangle-area wave that also reached Cumberland, Durham and Wake County towns.

t: Citrus County pauses data centers for a year; Deltona later drops its 800-acre plan
b: The 5–0 vote covers data center rezonings and permits. Deltona withdrew its Holder Industrial Park applications in June after the planning commission rejected the land-use change.

t: Simpson County's top official backs a statewide data center moratorium
b: Barnes said no Kentucky community is ready for a data center as his county fights TenKey's project in court.

t: Vance County rezones land along U.S. 158 for a possible Natelli data center
b: Natelli later filed plans for a 900 MW campus near Henderson, the state's largest active proposal.
iw: Land opened for a large campus

t: Apex adopts a one-year data center moratorium after a 250 MW plan is withdrawn
b: Natelli had pulled its New Hill Digital Campus beside the Harris nuclear plant on March 5, citing the town's zoning deliberations.

t: Fort Meade approves a 20-year deal for a 4.4 million sq ft hyperscale campus
b: Florida's commerce secretary called the project fundamentally flawed. Residents sued in May and started recall petitions, and the campus still needs a regional water permit.

t: Wendell pauses data centers through the end of 2026
b: The town acted with no data center proposed, citing undefined uses in its development ordinance; the pause also covers crypto mining.

t: West Virginia makes certified data centers pay county fire and ambulance fees
b: HB 5168, effective June 12, also entitles certified microgrids and data centers to county fire and police protection.

t: Appeals court upholds the voiding of the Digital Gateway rezoning
b: The unanimous ruling affirmed that the county's advertising defects voided the approvals and also sided with the American Battlefield Trust's separate suit. Prince William had spent more than $1.6 million defending the project.

t: Franklin planners approve TenKey's data center plan after a heated meeting
b: The unanimous vote cleared a preliminary plan for three 200,000 sq ft buildings with on-site gas power. A citizens group sued in April, and TenKey is suing Simpson County over its permit ordinance.

t: West Virginia certifies its first high-impact data center, Penzance's $4 billion Berkeley campus
b: The Bedington campus cleared the 90 MW threshold and is the first certified under the 2025 law that strips local zoning control and sends most new property tax revenue to the state.

t: Kings Mountain pauses data centers after a second proposal, then extends a year
b: The 182-day pause passed 5–2 in February; on Aug. 25 the council extended it into late August 2027.

t: Mississippi waives taxes for xAI's $20 billion Southaven data center
b: Reeves called it the largest economic development project in state history. The state waives sales, corporate income and franchise taxes, and Southaven and DeSoto County offer fee-in-lieu deals.

t: Bay County pauses data centers through January 2027
b: The moratorium was among the first in a Florida wave that later reached more than a dozen counties.

t: Bradley County limits data centers to special-impact zones with 3,000-foot buffers
b: The unanimous rules also cap property-line noise at 60 decibels; the only such zone at the time was a landfill.

t: Frederick County draws a larger data center zone than its planners advised
b: The council's map adds land around Quantum Frederick and the former Eastalco smelter, against a planning commission call to limit it to approved acreage. Residents launched a referendum petition.

t: Gates County adopts a data center moratorium
b: It came as a wave of local pauses built across North Carolina; more than 20 jurisdictions had pauses or bans by April 2026.

t: Georgia requires regional impact reviews for large data centers
b: Since November 2025, big data center proposals must go through a state Development of Regional Impact review with a public comment period.

t: Spanberger wins Virginia's governorship promising data centers will pay their fair share
b: She won 57–43 as Democrats took full control of state government, after a campaign in which rising power bills and data center growth were central themes.

t: Franklin residents protest a proposed AI data center at a planning meeting
b: The fight over TenKey's plan for three 200,000 sq ft buildings with on-site gas power has since moved to court.

t: Developers withdraw the Project Accelerate data center in Matthews
b: The five-building plan on 123 acres along East John Street drew fierce opposition over power use, taxes and noise before a scheduled Oct. 13 vote.

t: Earle-Sears says data centers are here to stay, blaming clean energy rules for bills
b: The Republican nominee for governor backed Youngkin's push for more data centers and an all-of-the-above energy policy, while Spanberger said developers must pay their fair share.

t: Frederick County confines data centers to a special overlay zone, 5–2
b: Data centers and their substations may only be built where the overlay is applied, after a June law cut eligible land from about 5,000 acres to 4,200.
iw: Data centers confined to one zone

t: Mississippi grants tax breaks for AVAIO's $6 billion Brandon campus
b: MDA approved the data center tax exemption, and Rankin County and Brandon are adding infrastructure upgrades and local incentives for the 175-acre Taurus site.

t: Tract drops its $30 billion Mooresville data center after community backlash
b: The plan for land owned by Dale Earnhardt's widow drew opposition over water and power use; the mayor said no other data center requests were active.

t: Judge voids the Prince William Digital Gateway rezoning
b: Judge Kimberly Irving ruled the county's notices for the December 2023 hearings broke state and county law, halting the 2,100-acre, 37-building corridor. An appeals court later barred construction during the appeal.

t: Monroe County rejects a 900-acre data center campus near Bolingbroke
b: The unanimous vote followed a planning board recommendation to deny the 1.1 GW proposal after hundreds of residents in red shirts turned out.

t: Fauquier planners recommend denying the Gigaland campus near Remington, 4–1
b: The seven-building, 2.2 million sq ft plan was later withdrawn twice, most recently in August 2026, and two other Remington-area data center applications were pulled within a month.

t: Richmond County approves secret tax breaks for Amazon's $10 billion campus
b: Commissioners rezoned and sold county land and approved 20-year property tax breaks for the unnamed Project Blue Marlin without disclosing it was a data center until Amazon was announced.

t: York County raises height limits for QTS's $8 billion data center campus
b: QTS said lower-water cooling systems needed taller buildings. The change followed a 2023 fee-in-lieu deal at a reduced 4% assessment with extra credits over 40 years.

t: Fort Meade rezones 1,164 acres for data centers with a $150 million tax break
b: The June 2025 approvals for Stonebridge's campus on former phosphate land include a 10-year tax break tied to more than $2.6 billion in planned investment.

t: Atlas withdraws its Bartow County data center campus after planners recommend denial
b: The withdrawal came the day before the county's sole commissioner was to rule; the planning commission had voted 6–1 against it in April.

t: Pittsylvania rejects Balico's gas-powered data center campus, 6–1
b: The board first refused Balico's request to withdraw, so the developer cannot refile a similar plan for a year. The original proposal paired 84 data centers with a 3,500 MW gas plant.

t: Bills to rewrite Mississippi's data center tax rules and power contracts die
b: HB 1239 died in conference and SB 3168 in committee; HB 1184, which would have allowed special large-customer power contracts, also died.

t: Spartanburg County backs incentives for the $2.8 billion Valara data center
b: County records list about 27 expected but not required jobs. The site later sought to expand on-site gas generation from about 50 MW to 450 MW, prompting state and court challenges.

t: Berkeley County planners approve a concept plan for two data center buildings
b: The project spans Berkeley and Jefferson counties; the March approval covered the Berkeley portion.

t: Maryland approves 172 diesel backup generators for Aligned's Frederick campus
b: The approval came after the 2024 streamlining law exempted backup generators from the state's power plant certificate, the requirement that had earlier stalled the project.

t: Twiggs County rezones land for a data center despite opposition
b: Residents have sued, alleging the county broke its own rules in approving the rezoning.

t: West Virginia approves air permits for the Adams Fork data center power plants
b: TransGas plans off-grid gas plants and an ammonia plant in Mingo County to power data centers; residents later sued in federal court.

t: Fairfax County tightens data center zoning with setbacks and Metro buffers
b: The September 2024 amendments require fully enclosed equipment, 200-foot setbacks from homes and a one-mile buffer from Metrorail stations. Only applications complete before July 16, 2024, were grandfathered.
iw: Tighter rules in a core market
